summary: Igbo-style goat head, cooked until tender and tossed in a thick, spiced palm-oil sauce with utazi and onions.
story: Isi ewu means "goat head" in Igbo and is a well-known delicacy from south-eastern Nigeria. It is served at celebrations, bars and restaurants, often in the evening with a cold drink.

items.name: Goat head, cleaned and singed
items.note: cut into chunks by your butcher

items.name: Potash (kaun)
items.note: mixed with 3 tbsp water, see swaps

steps.title: Prepare the head
steps.text: Rinse the goat head chunks well and check that all hair has been singed off. Wash again under cold running water.

steps.title: Boil until tender
steps.text: Place in a pot with the quartered onion, cubes and salt, cover with water and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or pressure-cook for 45 minutes. It is ready when the meat and skin are soft and the bone pulls away easily.

steps.title: Drain and chop
steps.text: Lift out the meat and let it cool slightly. Chop into bite-size pieces, removing any small bone fragments. Keep about 1/2 cup of the stock.

steps.title: Make the potash liquid
steps.text: Let the potash water settle and pour off only the clear liquid, leaving any grit behind. A small spoonful is all you need to thicken the palm oil.

steps.title: Thicken the palm oil
steps.text: Warm the palm oil gently in a pot, add about 1 tbsp of the clear potash liquid, and stir until it turns thick, creamy and a lighter orange, about 2 to 3 minutes. Do not allow it to boil.

steps.title: Add seasonings
steps.text: Stir in the ehuru, crayfish, scotch bonnet, cube and chopped onion. Loosen with a spoonful of stock if the sauce is too stiff.

steps.title: Fold in the goat
steps.text: Add the hot goat meat and stir until fully coated. Add the utazi and sliced onion, check salt, and serve warm, ideally in a wooden bowl.

tips: Buy the head already cleaned and singed, and check for hair.
Potash needs care: start with a little and taste.
Keep the sauce warm, not boiling, after thickening.
A pressure cooker saves well over an hour.

swaps.swap: Goat shoulder with bone plus a little tripe, or cow foot, gives a similar rich texture. It will be less gelatinous.
A pinch of baking soda dissolved in water; use sparingly.
Endive or a few rocket leaves for a bitter note.
